name: Question 6
problem: Which of the following matrices has a rank of $4?$
worked_solution:
First, notice that a matrix of rank $4$ must have at least $4$ columns and at least $4$ rows. 
So, we disregard the following matrices:

- $B$ since it has only $3$ rows.

- $D$ since it has only $3$ columns (and only $3$ rows).

- $E$ since it has only $3$ coumns.

Also, the matrix must have $4$ pivot columns. As we can see, the matrix $C$ has exactly $4$ pivot columns, while the matrix $A$ has only $2$ pivot columns. So, $\text{rank}(C)=4$ and $\text{rank}(A)=2.$

Therefore, the correct answer is the matrix $C.$

Question 6
?

Which of the following matrices has a rank of 4?

a
E=[120000001000]
b
B=[15001012−3000210]
c
D=[121020006]
d
C=[14−8000−23−11001−100000000004]
e
A=[10310−1−7200000000]
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that a matrix of rank 4 must have at least 4 columns and at least 4 rows. So, we disregard the following matrices:

  • B since it has only 3 rows.

  • D since it has only 3 columns (and only 3 rows).

  • E since it has only 3 coumns.

Also, the matrix must have 4 pivot columns. As we can see, the matrix C has exactly 4 pivot columns, while the matrix A has only 2 pivot columns. So, rank(C)=4 and rank(A)=2.

Therefore, the correct answer is the matrix C.
